text:
maria: quick follow-up from the fp/int4 tradeoffs RFC — thinking about a runtime "introspective gating" idea where the model/runtime can downgrade/upgrade precision mid-request based on a cheap quality signal. want to capture tradeoffs and API boundaries before i write a short proposal

akshay: sounds interesting. is the quality signal a learned head, logit-stability metric, or an external eval reranker?

maria: leaning toward a lightweight heuristic we can compute from logits + kv-cache divergence so it's cheap. fallback to a small teacher reranker only when the heuristic flags low confidence.

rachel: curious about latency P95 impact. switching precision mid-token sounds expensive (heap/allocator churn). do we expect a full kernel swap or just choose next-layer precision?

maria: good point — target design: precompile compatible kernels for fp8/int8/4bit that can be hot-swapped with minimal state copy; actual gating should happen at chunk boundaries (e.g., every N tokens) to avoid per-token syscall spikes.

jorge: operational questions: how do we record this in traces/metrics? need to surface "precision_changes_per_request" and correlate with quality regressions. also who owns rollout policy (platform vs model owner)?

akshay: propose runtime emits events: PRECISION_DECISION {request_id, token_index_range, old_profile, new_profile, signal_value}. we keep a per-route sampling to capture full logits for post-hoc eval.

maria: API boundary idea: keep the existing generation API but add an opt-in header/param e.g. "x-redwood-precision-gating: auto|off|manual". when manual, SDK can request explicit precision sets per-chunk. default off for now.

rachel: for manual mode we need a compact contract: an ordered list of (start_token, precision_profile) so model-serving doesn't need to do heavy parsing. also we should accept the list in token indices or prefix hashes.

akshay: rollout plan: 1) internal A/B on non-critical customer routes with heavy sampling, 2) enable auto for canary pool with strict SLO guardrails, 3) expose in console with cost/latency estimates.

maria: quality monitoring: define a small default eval-suite (N prompts per model) and a per-request quick-check that runs a cheap LM-consistency test (e.g., compare top-5 token overlap across precisions). if overlap < T then mark for rerank.

jorge: safety net: always keep a fallback policy to prioritized older model variant (higher-precision) if the request fails or latency spikes. implement a credit/budget so we only do expensive fallbacks for a bounded fraction.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: created rollout checklist issue #4521 and a canary job template (canary-precision-gating)

akshay: possible kernel-level optimization: maintain per-GPU reserved buffer for quant state so switching profiles rebinds pointers instead of copying. need memory-accounting changes though.

maria: we should separate concerns: runtime implements low-latency switch, policy engine decides when, and eval infra provides the thresholds. keep the policy declarative (yaml) so product can tweak without code.

rachel: edge case: streaming clients. if we change precision mid-stream, do we resend prior tokens or annotate stream chunks with the precision used? probably annotate — resending is costly. note: some clients rely on exact token IDs for streaming reassembly.

maria: annotate streams with `precision_profile` metadata at chunk boundaries. add compatibility mode to forbid mid-stream changes per-route.

akshay: for experiments, mock the gating using offline traces: replay requests at different profiles and compute overlap + latency delta. that gives a quick estimator before runtime rollout.

maria: action items: akshay — prototype event schema and kernel pointer-binding plan; rachel — simulate cost/latency with replay traces and streaming compatibility tests; jorge — telemetry/console metrics + rollout policy draft. i'll write the short RFC follow-up with these decisions and a minimal API patch.

jorge: acked, i'll include a couple of Grafana panels we can expose: "precision_changes/sec", "avg_latency_by_profile", "quality_overlap_pct".

maria: thank you all. i'll ping when the draft lands. :thumbsup:

akshay: +1, excited to see numbers.

rachel: thanks — will start on the replay harness tomorrow.

ops-bot: note: scheduled a sync 2pm Thu if you want to walk the RFC.
